subject: Business
title: The Innovator's Dilemma
description: Learn The Innovator's Dilemma in one minute.

hook.text: Kodak invented the digital camera in 1975 — then buried it to protect film sales.

buildup.text: Clayton Christensen called this the innovator's dilemma: successful firms can't disrupt themselves.

discovery.text: Incumbents serve profitable customers with small improvements. Disruption starts in low-end niches.

twist.text: The disruptor's product is worse at first. Incumbents laugh — until the technology catches up.

climax.text: Netflix mailed DVDs while Blockbuster had 9,000 stores. Blockbuster is gone.

punchline.text: The biggest threat is the product you're too successful to build.

quiz.question: Why do incumbents often fail to adopt disruptive technology?
options: It threatens their profitable existing business

details.summary: Clayton Christensen's Innovator's Dilemma explains why startups can defeat industry giants. Incumbents rationally focus on their best customers and ignore disruptive technologies that initially serve only small markets.
details.whyItMatters: The Innovator's Dilemma is the most important strategic framework for startup founders because it reveals exactly how small companies can defeat seemingly invincible incumbents by targeting markets they cannot rationally pursue.
takeaways: Incumbents rationally ignore disruptive technologies that initially serve small markets
Startups win by targeting customers that large companies cannot profitably serve
By the time incumbents recognize the threat, the startup has built insurmountable lead

faq.question: How can startups use the Innovator's Dilemma as a strategy?
faq.answer: Target customers that incumbents cannot profitably serve due to their cost structures. Build a product that is simpler and cheaper, not better by mainstream standards. Improve rapidly while incumbents ignore you. By the time you serve mainstream customers, you have years of learning advantage.

faq.question: What industries are most vulnerable to disruption right now?
faq.answer: Industries with high costs, poor customer experience, and significant friction in delivery. Healthcare, education, legal services, insurance, and financial services all have characteristics that match Christensen's disruption pattern.
